must_identify.item: The new api pods exit because the name redis does not resolve
must_identify.evidence: The api container tries to resolve REDIS_HOST=redis at startup; with ndots:5 the resolver tries redis.shop.svc.cluster.internal, redis.svc.cluster.internal, redis.cluster.internal, then bare redis — all fail — producing: redis connection failed (attempt 1/5): [Errno -2] Name does not resolve ... The process then calls sys.exit(1)

must_identify.item: The cause is the pod's dnsPolicy None / dnsConfig search domains (cluster.internal), not REDIS_HOST, the redis Service or CoreDNS
must_identify.evidence: But the search domain suffix is wrong: it uses cluster.internal instead of the cluster's actual domain cluster.local. ... Redis itself is healthy and unrelated: service redis (ClusterIP 10.96.245.188) has a live endpoint ... This is purely a DNS-resolution break introduced by the new pod spec, not a Redis outage.

notes: The RCA explicitly clears the redis Service and confirms the nameserver IP is correct, which clears CoreDNS by implication. It treats REDIS_HOST=redis as a valid short name without stating outright that it is fine. The fix offers removing the dnsConfig, correcting the domains to cluster.local, or rollout undo, and all three are acceptable.
